title: How long it lasted; the station connection and Quaker flour transcriptions
summary: The XEPN work lasted about a year, until the stock of transcriptions was repeated. A Minnesota flour company also hired them for 32 transcriptions, and they were always unidentified.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. For how many years did you work for the border stations in this capacity?

Just about one year. I don't know what happened then. I think they started repeating what we had already done. We'd had it had a backlog enough, so that was it. They could even turn those on today and do the same thing if a man would think of it.
Were you with any other station besides XCPN?
No, that's all. And that's just because the fellow there at Crazy Waters had bought some stock.
They bought some stock on the station?

An XCPN station. Oh. And was able to, you see, just import these little ones. He'd hire us cheap. And we were good musicians. Just to get readily there, conveniently, at this recording studio at Mineral Wells. Mm-hmm.
What was the initial contact with anybody from the station?
I have no idea. Oh, yes. Old Quaker Flower Company from Minnesota. One summer came down and made 32 transcriptions for use there.
In Minnesota. In Minnesota. Old Quaker.

No, O-Q-A-C-K-A or something like that. Old Quaker Flower or something. That may not be the right name. It sounds suspicious, but I think that's what it was. A flower company from Minnesota hired us to make 32 transcriptions.
And these were then the only two stations? That I recall. Yeah. But that was using a border station technique with an inland station. Mm-hmm. And were you again unidentified on those?
